source.title: A new initialisation to Control Gradients in Sinusoidal Neural network
source.authors: Andrea Combette; Antoine Venaille; Nelly Pustelnik

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper and appendices. The version header gives v2 dated 11 May 2026; no text appears cut off.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures how initialization affects gradient propagation, depth scaling, and training error in sinusoidal networks, which bears on V4. It uses a different architecture and tasks from the claim versions' classification benchmarks.
record.gate_note: The paper reports initialization comparisons and training-error results for function fitting, image reconstruction, and PDE tasks. These are the study's own results. Prior-work findings in its introduction and references are not included as rows. Figure-only comparisons without textual outcome descriptions are not separately reconstructed as numeric rows.
record.test_reason: The study extends activation-specific initialization analysis to plain sinusoidal networks. Its own gradient-scaling experiments, NTK analysis and training-error results bear on V4. Most reconstruction benefits concern generalization rather than training speed.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors distinguish fixing Jacobian variance to control gradients from targeting vanishing pre-activation variance to control the spectrum. Their principal demonstrated task benefits concern reconstruction and generalization; they also argue that initialization shapes training dynamics through the NTK.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes a new SIREN weight and bias initialization, compared with the original SIREN scheme and other INR methods; it does not reproduce the cited CIFAR classification recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization scheme, network depth, and width affect training error, generalization, noise, and high-frequency content. The σa = 0 and σa = 1 initializations differ in spectral growth; finite-width behavior includes a reported performance cost.

fits_no_version.finding: Small-width image reconstruction retains lower noise under the proposed initialization but suffers substantial performance degradation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Spectral regularization through initialization has width-dependent reconstruction costs.

fits_no_version.finding: Depth 40 improves proposed-initialization reconstruction; the other schemes show differing high-frequency artifacts and generalization behavior.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization controls the depth dependence of spectral artifacts and interpolation quality in sinusoidal representations.

fits_no_version.finding: Denoising improves clean-image SNR and MSE while leaving substantially greater noisy-target training loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The proposed initialization provides implicit spectral regularization that trades noisy-target fit for clean-signal reconstruction.

fits_no_version.finding: Burgers initialization comparisons are similar, with original SIREN most favorable; other PDE tasks favor the proposed scheme.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization benefits for PDE reconstruction depend on the equation and target spectrum.

record.problems: Most task-specific quantitative comparisons are figure-only in the supplied text, without exact values. The theoretical derivation uses infinite-width/depth limits, while finite-width experiments report a severe performance cost for the proposed initialization. Experiments concern INR function fitting, reconstruction and PDE tasks, not CIFAR classification.
record.rows_left_out: No numeric values were read from plots where the supplied text did not state them. Other figure-only comparisons in Figures 2, 4, 6, 11–19, and 20–21 are not individually extracted unless accompanied by a textual result relevant to V4. The denoising and Burgers outcomes are summarized under fits_no_version because the versions do not name those measures or settings.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V4. No plot coordinates were reconstructed. Figure-only omissions were declared, but Section 4 contains explicit textual results essential to assessing V4 that the record does not capture. Generalization degradation and spectral noise should not be treated as training failure.

conditions.value: setting of Figure 2; exact depth not stated here

rows.measure: Image fitting performance and noise level
rows.value: Lower noise level even at small width; severely harms performance.
rows.note: The paper explicitly reports a tradeoff: noise remains lower, although performance is severely harmed.

rows.subject: SIREN (σa = 0)
rows.operation_detail: Compared initialization methods at depths L = 10 and L = 40 in the image-fitting experiment; setting follows Figure 2.
rows.measure: Image-fitting performance and effective noise level
rows.baseline: Same proposed initialization at L = 10 and competing initializations at L = 40
rows.value: Increasing depth to L = 40 improves performance and further reduces effective noise level.
rows.note: The reported depth comparison supports trainability under this initialization in the tested image-fitting setting.
rows.check: Improved image performance and reduced noise at depth 40 do not establish faster optimization or lower training error. The text does not separate training fit from reconstruction quality.

rows.subject: SIREN (σa = 1)
rows.operation_detail: Compared initialization methods at depths L = 10 and L = 40 in the image-fitting experiment; setting follows Figure 2.

rows.value: Large-depth performance is described as surprisingly good, despite clear growth of high-frequency components with depth.
rows.note: The paper qualifies the depth result: performance can remain good while high-frequency content grows.
rows.check: Good reconstruction despite high-frequency growth measures spectral and reconstruction behavior, rather than V4's training-speed or trainable-depth effect.

relationships.condition: Gradient-preservation mechanism in plain sinusoidal networks at initialization
relationships.reason: Based on Section 4 text, not existing rows: the new initializations maintain input gradients across depth, whereas original SIREN gradients grow exponentially and PyTorch gradients vanish; NTK analysis connects initialization to learning dynamics.
relationships.display_finding: The new initializations maintained input gradients across depth, whereas original SIREN gradients grew exponentially and PyTorch gradients vanished.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Gradient-preservation mechanism in plain sinusoidal networks at initialization
source_check.reason: Section 4 reports depth-stable input gradients under the proposed initializations and connects their NTK scaling to learning dynamics, contrasting with vanishing gradients and slow convergence under PyTorch initialization. This supports the specified mechanism; it does not establish a measured training-speed advantage.

relationships.condition: Training acceleration versus gradient stability in sinusoidal networks
relationships.reason: Based on Section 4 text, not existing rows: original SIREN's exploding gradients accompany faster training with depth. Stable gradients therefore do not establish a general speed advantage; the reported benefit also involves interpolation quality.
relationships.display_finding: Original SIREN's exploding gradients accompanied faster training with depth, while the stable initialization's reported benefits also involved interpolation quality.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Training acceleration versus gradient stability in sinusoidal networks
source_check.reason: Section 4 explicitly associates original SIREN's exploding gradients with acceleration as depth increases. This shows that gradient stability is unnecessary for acceleration, but V4 does not claim necessity. The cited result does not establish failure of the stable initialization's claimed speed or trainable-depth benefit; lack of a demonstrated comparative advantage is not a scope limitation.
